Never in a game have I ever felt more like prey instead of hunter.

The game is fantastic.

And boy is it creepy. Enemies are almost human, but with such alienly warped features that it looks like God found some corpses, smooshed them around like clay, and gave them life again. With the unsettling enemy design and your complete inability to fight back, I'd say this is the scariest game I've ever played (though for reference I found the claymation segments of the Amanda Bynes Show FAR FAR more pants shittingly traumitizing than any horror movie, so maybe that just says more about me than the game (hah!)).

It's also tad bit on the short side (steam says I have less than 4 hours at completion).
It's definitely a quality over quantity thing.

Gameplay is mostly side-scrolling with 3D elements puzzle/platformer game -- very similar to Inside, Limbo, or Unravel if you've played those games.

I usually would be more hesitant to recommend a game with such a short playtime -- but this is such a unique and quality experience, that I wholly recommend it to all who enjoy these type of games.

From when this game came out I was captivated by it's story and unique visuals. It has only been recently that I have been able to experience this masterpiece that sparked an indie game franchise that has spread to mobile devices. Little Nightmares is not afraid of creating it's own niche.

Aesthetically this game is a joy, it oozes mystery and sinister undertones. The soundtrack and audio in general were splendid. I enjoyed my time with the game, but something felt missing. I am absolutely unable to pinpoint what it was, but something about the experience felt hollow.

8/10

Little Nightmares is a masterclass in atmospheric horror that replaces dialogue with visceral storytelling. Navigating the Maw as Six is a haunting experience where the grotesque character designs and oppressive soundscapes turn every room into a tense survival puzzle. Since I took the time to unlock every single achievement, I can safely say that the level design is incredibly rewarding to master. Conquering the "Hard to the Core" challenge was especially satisfying and showed me just how much detail went into this world. It is a rare game that perfectly balances childhood vulnerability with a dark, cinematic polish. Achieving 100% completion felt like the perfect way to truly appreciate this beautifully twisted masterpiece.

This game is atmospheric and has a wonderful and engaging score. It can be played again and again for both players that want to find something new, and for folks that like games which feel as immersive interactive movies. Little Nightmares set design is original and inspired, as are the beings one encounters within the walls of The Maw. If one is looking for an engaging story, told in great part by its setting, look no further!

This game is an absolute masterpiece, true visual storytelling, I really can't fault it. Even if you don't like stressful games that much, it is still so worth it, even just to experience the atmosphere, since the sound design and lighting are phenomenal. 11/10 - would absolutely play again!

I am having fun with the game, unfortunately trying to do the Kitchen Hand achievement with the 3 ingredients is very buggy I had to reset a couple times (5-6 times) since the carrot fell next to the cooking pot on the ledge and they you were not able to re-grab these on the higher ledge ... This has put me off the game for a bit before going back to it and 100%'ing this one ...

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Amazing Little Horror Adventure!

Little Nightmares is a really good atmospheric horror game with a unique art style, creepy environments, and an interesting story. The puzzles and mini-game style sections are fun, and exploring the Maw keeps the experience engaging.

The only downside for me is the controller guidance/controls. Some parts aren't explained very clearly, especially when figuring out what button or action to use, which can make certain sections confusing or frustrating.

Apart from that, it's a great game with excellent atmosphere, sound design, puzzles, and creepy characters. Definitely worth playing if you enjoy short horror and puzzle-adventure games.

Overall: 9/10 🎮🔥

The game nails the atmosphere and the spookiness.

But that's about it.

The actual gameplay is okay but I just found it frustrating a lot. The platforming is 2.5D, which for me is the worst of both worlds, because you have to play around things by going towards/away from the screen, but the forced perspective makes it annoying to judge positioning.

The controls, especially grabbing just feel weird, I was never certain when I was in position to grab/throw something properly.

Which all would have been fine except then the game added "stealth". Except there's zero indication or feedback about what causes the weird monsters to be able to catch you - it more feels like they're scripted to ignore certain spots which forces you to play a certain way, and that gets annoying fast.

And then you have to do puzzle solving and stealth in the same sections, and you're in a hurry, and then you die because you ran into something or failed to grab something and it's just annoying to redo.

So I gave up on the game.

Maybe if you're better at platforming you might not have these problems, in which case definitely a good game, because like I said, the atmosphere and visuals are really spot on.

Fullscreen have scale problems. To fix resolution you need to activate borderless window mode:
- Find the game location on your system (manage > browse local files)
- Go to <path-to-game>\Atlas\Saved\Config\WindowsNoEditor\
- Open GameUserSettings.ini with notepad
- Add or modify FullscreenMode=1
- Save changes

This isn't usually my type of game but for some reason I can't help but love it. It features some simple puzzle throughout the area's.

It's a really short game and only took me around 10 hours to complete the main game and DLC. It's one of those games that does environmental story telling the best since there is no dialogue in the game. The horror aspect of the game is creepy and eerie. There is no jump scares from what I recall, but its the design of the characters that put you on edge... and if you really pay attention to the backgrounds in certain areas you'd find that maybe you're not always alone exploring the Maw :). 

After finishing the main game I was left confused but not in a disappointed way, just in a way were I was left with more welcomed questions than answers, but after finishing the DLC I was left depressed and shocked with more answers to the questions I had from the main ending. 

Overall its a solid game and can't wait to play Little Nightmares 2, but after finishing everything I think I might hold off on it and play something a little more lighthearted because if the second game is anything like the first then I don't know if playing back to back depressing games is the move. 

It's a solid 9/10 with my only complaint is that sometimes the controls felt a little jank, but it's a very minor complaint.

First time playing this genre, and I enjoyed it a lot. The horror atmosphere was so immersive, and I really liked stealthing, and the running sequences. The game doesn’t overstay its welcome at all. The graphics are amazing, and the gameplay feels very responsive. The only issue I had was with depth perception it can be tricky sometimes, but I got used to it quickly. I also like how the game doesn’t demand too much from the player, letting you just enjoy the ride and get immersed in the environment without worrying too much about complex mechanics.

I still haven’t played any of the DLCs, but I’d like to get to them in the future, as well as work on getting all the achievements for the game.

I got the game for free on Steam a few years ago when it was available to claim.
